## Review Summary

This branch is very small and the intent is clear: permit `openai_async` as a valid `ModelConfig` provider and align the live provider test with that value. However, the change only updates validation; `ModelConfig` still serializes every provider back to the `openai-compat` scheme, so the new provider does not round-trip correctly and can be misreported or rewritten downstream.

**Files Reviewed:** 3
**Findings:** 0 Critical, 1 Warning, 1 Suggestion

## Findings

### Critical Findings

None.

### Warning Findings

[W-01] `ModelConfig` rewrites `openai_async` back to `openai-compat` when serialized
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: src/domain/value_objects/model_config.py
Lines: 100-116
Description: The PR adds `openai_async` to the validation allow-list, but `to_string()` still hardcodes `scheme = "openai-compat"` for every instance. That means a config created as `ModelConfig(name="...", provider="openai_async")` serializes as an OpenAI-compatible URL instead of preserving the async provider. This is not only a cosmetic mismatch: `src/infrastructure/prompts/prompt_handler.py` records `request.model_config.to_string()` as `model_used`, so any async-backed request will now be logged or persisted as the wrong provider string. If that serialized value is reused later, it routes back through the `openai_compatible` path instead of `openai_async`, defeating the purpose of the new provider value.
Suggestion: Make serialization provider-aware. Preserve `openai_async` with its own scheme (or a documented alias such as `openai-async`) and add matching parse logic if an alias is chosen. The round-trip invariant should hold: `ModelConfig.from_string(str(config))` should retain the same provider.

### Suggestions

[S-01] Add round-trip tests for the new provider, not only direct construction
Category: Testing
Severity: Suggestion
File: tests/unit/test_model_config.py
Lines: 84-89
Description: The new unit test verifies only that direct construction with `provider="openai_async"` no longer raises. It does not cover the code path that most of the application uses, `ModelConfig.from_string(...)`, nor the serializer path that converts configs back to strings. Because of that gap, the current suite would still pass with the broken serialization behavior above.
Suggestion: Add focused tests that assert both parsing and serialization preserve the async provider, for example `ModelConfig.from_string("openai_async://test-model")` and `str(ModelConfig(name="test-model", provider="openai_async"))`.

## Overall Assessment

Not ready for merge yet. The validation change is incomplete because the value object still collapses the new provider back to the legacy scheme during serialization, which can silently mislabel or reroute async model configurations. Once provider-aware round-trip behavior is implemented and covered by unit tests, this PR should be safe to merge.
